No. The Moon’s center is about **6.9° below the astronomical horizon**, so the entire lunar disk is well below it and cannot be seen directly, regardless of its 82% illumination or the clear sky.

Local terrain, buildings, and atmospheric refraction would only make matters worse; ordinary near-horizon refraction is far too small to lift an object almost 7° into view. You would need to wait for the Moon to rise above the **local** horizon.
